html:
Single-Tooth Implants in Wauwatosa

Losing one tooth can have a bigger impact than you might expect. A gap in your smile can affect how you chew, change your bite, make you hesitant to smile, and eventually contribute to changes in the bone where the tooth once stood. A single-tooth dental implant in Wauwatosa can replace the missing tooth from root to crown, creating a stable, natural-looking restoration without relying on neighboring teeth for support.

At MidTown Dental Care, Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego provide comprehensive dental implant treatment in one convenient location. From your initial evaluation and advanced 3D imaging to bone grafting when needed, implant placement, and your final custom restoration, our team can coordinate each stage of your care.

Whether you recently lost a tooth or have lived with a gap for years, we can help you determine whether a single dental implant is the right solution to rebuild your smile.

Schedule a Dental Implant Consultation

What Is a Single-Tooth Dental Implant?

A single-tooth dental implant is designed to replace a single missing tooth without relying on the surrounding teeth for support.

The restoration typically has three main components:

The dental implant is a small post placed into the jawbone where the natural tooth root was previously located.

The abutment connects the implant to the final restoration.

The dental crown is the visible portion of the replacement tooth and is designed to complement your surrounding smile.

After the implant is placed, the surrounding bone heals and integrates with the implant. Once the implant has achieved appropriate stability, the final restoration can be completed.

The result is a replacement tooth designed to provide the appearance and function of a natural tooth while receiving support from the jaw rather than adjacent teeth.

When Should You Replace a Missing Tooth?

If a missing tooth is not especially visible, it can be tempting to leave the space alone. However, replacing a tooth is not always just a cosmetic decision.

After tooth loss, nearby teeth can gradually shift toward the open space. This movement may affect your bite and create areas that are more difficult to keep clean. Depending on the location of the missing tooth, chewing may also become less efficient.

The jawbone in the area can change as well. Natural tooth roots stimulate the surrounding bone through normal biting and chewing. When the root is no longer present, the bone in that area may gradually decrease.

A dental implant replaces the missing root and transfers forces into the surrounding jawbone, helping maintain support in the area.

Benefits of Replacing One Missing Tooth With a Dental Implant

For the right patient, a single dental implant offers several important advantages.

It Does Not Depend on Neighboring Teeth

One of the most significant differences between a dental implant and a traditional dental bridge is the source of support for the restoration.

A traditional bridge generally uses neighboring teeth as anchors for the replacement tooth. Those teeth must be prepared to accommodate dental crowns.

A single dental implant stands independently. Healthy neighboring teeth generally do not need to be altered to support the implant restoration.

It Looks Natural

The final dental crown is customized to work with the surrounding smile. Its shape, proportions, and appearance are planned to create a natural-looking result.

This can be especially important when replacing a tooth that is visible when you smile.

It Restores Function

A missing tooth can make chewing certain foods more difficult or cause you to favor one side of your mouth.

Once appropriately healed and restored, an implant-supported tooth is designed to provide stable function for everyday biting and chewing.

It Helps Support the Jawbone

Because the implant is positioned within the jaw, it interacts with the surrounding bone in a way that a traditional tooth-supported bridge cannot.

This is one reason dental implants are often considered when planning a long-term solution for a missing tooth.

It Can Provide Long-Term Value

Dental implants are designed as a durable tooth-replacement solution. With excellent oral hygiene, regular dental care, and appropriate maintenance, an implant can remain functional for many years.

The crown attached to the implant can experience normal wear over time and may eventually need maintenance or replacement.

Dental Implant or Bridge: Which Is Better for One Missing Tooth?

Patients frequently ask whether they should choose a dental implant or a dental bridge.

Both can effectively replace a missing tooth, but they accomplish the goal differently.

A traditional bridge fills the space using a replacement tooth supported by crowns on neighboring teeth. This may be an appropriate solution when those neighboring teeth already need crowns or when implant surgery is not recommended.

A dental implant replaces the missing tooth independently. Because it receives its support from the jawbone, neighboring healthy teeth generally do not need to be prepared to support the restoration.

There are other considerations as well, including bone availability, gum health, treatment timeline, cost, medical history, and the condition of surrounding teeth.

There is no universal answer that applies to every patient. During your consultation at MidTown Dental Care, we can evaluate your smile and explain the advantages and considerations of both options.

What Is the Single-Tooth Dental Implant Process?

Your treatment is planned around your individual needs rather than a one-size-fits-all timeline.

1. Implant Consultation and Evaluation

We begin by examining the missing-tooth area, surrounding teeth, gums, bite, and overall oral health. We also discuss how the tooth was lost and how long it has been missing.

Advanced imaging helps us evaluate the underlying jawbone and anatomical structures that cannot be fully assessed during a visual examination.

2. Treatment Planning

Our doctors use the information gathered during your examination and imaging to determine the appropriate implant position and develop your treatment plan.

If another tooth is still present but cannot be saved, an extraction may be part of the process.

3. Bone Grafting When Necessary

Some patients have enough healthy bone to proceed with implant treatment without grafting. Others may need additional bone support.

Bone loss can occur after a tooth has been missing for an extended period or because of infection, periodontal disease, trauma, or other factors.

If bone grafting is recommended, MidTown Dental Care can incorporate it into your overall treatment plan.

4. Dental Implant Placement

The implant is carefully positioned in the planned location within the jawbone.

MidTown Dental Care also offers advanced Yomi robot-assisted dental implant technology. Yomi provides real-time guidance to the dentist based on the digital treatment plan while the dentist remains in control of the procedure.

5. Healing

After placement, the implant needs time to heal and integrate with the surrounding bone. The length of this phase varies depending on your health, bone quality, implant location, and whether additional procedures were required.

6. Your Final Dental Crown

Once the implant has achieved appropriate stability, the final restoration can be completed.

Your implant crown is designed to restore the appearance and function of the missing tooth so it fits comfortably into your smile.

Complete Implant Treatment at MidTown Dental Care

Having multiple phases of dental implant treatment does not necessarily mean visiting multiple practices.

At MidTown Dental Care, we provide comprehensive implant care from implant placement through the final restoration, including bone grafting when necessary.

Keeping treatment coordinated within one practice allows our doctors to plan your care with the final result in mind from the beginning.

Our implant team includes Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego. Their combined experience, advanced technology, and comprehensive approach allow us to create personalized solutions for patients replacing missing teeth.

Dr. Crego alone brings more than 40 years of dental experience to the practice and has a particular interest in implant placement, crown and bridge dentistry, and incorporating dental technology into patient care.

Yomi Robot-Assisted Technology for Single-Tooth Implants

Precise planning is particularly important when replacing a single missing tooth because the implant must fit within the available space between neighboring teeth and align with the patient’s overall bite.

MidTown Dental Care uses Yomi robot-assisted technology for dental implant surgery.

Using a digitally planned implant position, Yomi provides real-time guidance and haptic feedback during the procedure. The dentist performs the surgery and remains in control, using the technology to help ensure the planned implant location, angle, and depth are maintained.

Our dedicated Yomi Robot-Assisted Dental Implants page explains this technology and its role in implant treatment in greater detail.

How Much Does a Single-Tooth Dental Implant Cost?

The cost of replacing one tooth with an implant depends on the treatment required.

Factors can include:

  • Whether the damaged tooth needs to be extracted
  • Amount of available jawbone
  • Whether bone grafting is necessary
  • Complexity of implant placement
  • Type of final restoration
  • Dental insurance benefits
  • Individual treatment needs

Because these factors vary, an examination is necessary to provide an accurate treatment estimate.

At your consultation, we’ll explain the recommended treatment and associated costs so you can make an informed decision.

Financing Your Dental Implant

Cost should be part of the treatment conversation from the beginning.

MidTown Dental Care offers several payment and financing options, including CareCredit, Cherry, and Sunbit. In-house financing is also available for certain procedures.

Please contact our team to discuss your current benefits and payment options. Our team can help you understand applicable benefits and available payment options before beginning treatment.

Ready to Replace Your Missing Tooth?

Schedule a consultation with our Wauwatosa dental team to find out whether a single-tooth dental implant is right for you.

Schedule an Implant Consultation

Single-Tooth Dental Implant FAQs

How long does a single-tooth dental implant last?

Dental implants are designed to be a long-term tooth-replacement option. With appropriate oral hygiene, professional dental care, and healthy habits, the implant itself can remain functional for many years. The dental crown attached to it may eventually require maintenance or replacement because of normal wear.

How long does it take to replace one tooth with an implant?

Treatment time varies. Patients who need an extraction, bone graft, or additional healing may have a longer timeline than someone who is ready for implant placement immediately. The implant also generally requires a healing period before the final restoration is completed.

Can I get an implant immediately after losing a tooth?

In some situations, an implant may be placed relatively soon after a tooth is removed. In others, healing or bone grafting may be recommended first. The condition of the socket, available bone, infection, and other clinical factors determine the appropriate timing.

Do I need a bone graft for one dental implant?

Not necessarily. Bone grafting is recommended when there is insufficient healthy bone to provide adequate support for the planned implant. Advanced imaging allows our doctors to evaluate your bone before treatment.

Is a single dental implant better than a bridge?

It depends on your circumstances. An implant can replace a missing tooth without relying on neighboring healthy teeth for support and can help maintain bone in the area where the tooth is missing. A bridge can also be an excellent option, particularly when neighboring teeth would benefit from crowns or when implant surgery is not appropriate. Your dentist can help you compare the two.

Does getting a single dental implant hurt?

The treatment area is numbed during implant placement to help keep you comfortable. Tenderness, swelling, or soreness can occur afterward. The amount and duration of discomfort vary, and we provide post-treatment instructions to help you manage recovery.

Will my implant tooth look like a real tooth?

The final crown is designed to blend with your smile and restore the appearance of the missing tooth. Factors such as its size, shape, proportions, and relationship to surrounding teeth are considered when planning the restoration.

Can a front tooth be replaced with a dental implant?

Dental implants can be used to replace front and back teeth when the patient is an appropriate candidate. Front-tooth implant treatment requires careful planning because the appearance of the gumline and final restoration is particularly important in the smile zone.

What happens if I don’t replace a missing tooth?

Potential changes can include movement of neighboring teeth, changes in bite, reduced chewing efficiency, and loss of bone in the area of the missing tooth. The effects vary depending on the tooth’s location and your overall oral health.

How do I know if I’m a candidate for a single-tooth implant?

Candidacy depends on factors such as your jawbone, gum health, overall health, oral hygiene, the location of the missing tooth, and certain lifestyle factors. The best way to know is to have a dental implant evaluation and appropriate imaging.

Replace Your Missing Tooth With Confidence

One missing tooth does not have to become a permanent gap in your smile.

At MidTown Dental Care, Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego provide comprehensive implant care in Wauwatosa, including advanced imaging, bone grafting when necessary, implant placement, Yomi robot-assisted technology, and final implant restorations.

If you’re considering a single-tooth dental implant in Wauwatosa, schedule a consultation at MidTown Dental Care, located at 8726 W. North Ave., Wauwatosa, WI 53226. We’ll evaluate your smile, explain your tooth-replacement options, and help you decide on the treatment that makes sense for you.

html:
Minimal Prep, Maximum Results

Are you seeking a quick, pain-free way to achieve a confident, dazzling smile? No-prep veneers in Wauwatosa are transforming cosmetic dentistry by offering patients a minimally invasive solution with stunning, natural-looking results. At MidTown Dental Care, our team is dedicated to helping you enhance your smile without the discomfort or downtime of traditional veneers. Discover how no-prep veneers at MidTown Dental Care can reshape your smile, boost your confidence, and preserve your natural teeth.

 What Are No-Prep Veneers?

No-prep veneers are ultra-thin shells made from high-quality porcelain or composite materials designed to cover the front surface of your teeth. Unlike traditional veneers, they require little to no reduction of your existing teeth. Instead of drilling, shaving, or extensive preparation, these veneers are bonded directly to your natural enamel.

Key Benefits of No-Prep Veneers

  • Preserves Natural Tooth Structure: We remove virtually no enamel, so your teeth remain as healthy and strong as possible.
  • No Anesthesia or Drilling Needed: The process is comfortable and typically pain-free, making it ideal for patients anxious about dental work.
  • Faster Results: No-prep veneers can be placed in fewer visits, allowing you to enjoy your new smile sooner.

Why Choose No-Prep Veneers?

Minimally Invasive

No-prep veneers eliminate the need for painful tooth shaving. Your natural enamel is largely untouched, preserving your tooth structure and reducing the risk of sensitivity or complications.

Instant Smile Makeover

No-prep veneers offer a rapid cosmetic transformation to cover stains, close small gaps, or mask minor misalignments. Right after your appointment, enjoy a brighter, more balanced smile.

Durable & Natural-Looking

Our veneers are crafted from advanced ceramic and composite materials that deliver the perfect balance of strength and translucency. They blend seamlessly with your natural teeth for a beautiful, authentic appearance.

Ideal for Busy Lifestyles

Life doesn’t slow down for a smile upgrade. With no-prep veneers, you benefit from a streamlined process with fewer appointments and minimal post-procedure discomfort, allowing you to get back to your day confidently.

The No-Prep Veneers Process at MidTown Dental Care

Choosing no-prep veneers with our Wauwatosa dentists is straightforward and patient-centered. Here’s what you can expect:

Consultation:

Meet with Dr. Russell for a digital smile assessment.

Discuss your smile goals and explore whether no-prep veneers are right for you.

Design:

Select the shade and shape that will best complement your features.

We use digital imaging to preview your future smile.

Bonding:

After minimal to no tooth preparation, your custom veneers are gently bonded to your teeth.

Most cases are completed in just 1–2 visits.

See the Results! 

Browse our Before & After Gallery to see real MidTown Dental Care patients in Wauwatosa who have transformed their smiles with no-prep veneers.

No-Prep Veneers vs. Traditional Veneers

Feature No-Prep Veneers Traditional Veneers
Tooth Preparation Minimal or none Requires enamel removal
Anesthesia Rarely needed Typically required
Treatment Time 1–2 visits 2–3 visits
Longevity 7–10 years (with proper care) 10–15 years (with proper care)
Cost Generally lower Generally higher
Reversibility Often reversible Permanent

Cost & Financing

No-prep veneers in Wauwatosa can be costly. MidTown Dental Care offers a range of affordable options, including:

  • Flexible Payment Plans: Choose CareCredit, Cherry, or Sunbit for manageable monthly payments.
  • Insurance Assistance: Our team can help you maximize dental benefits.
  • Exclusive Membership Discounts: Save even more with our in-house membership plan.

Affordable Options Available – Ask Our Team!

FAQs About No-Prep Veneers

Are no-prep veneers reversible? 

Since little to no enamel is removed, most no-prep veneers can be reversed if needed.

How long do they last? 

No-prep veneers typically last 7–10 years with proper oral hygiene and care.

Can they fix crooked teeth? 

No-prep veneers can address minor misalignments, but severe orthodontic concerns may require other treatments.

Why Choose MidTown Dental Care?

Choosing MidTown Dental Care means trusting a team with:

  • Proven Expertise: Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego are highly skilled in cosmetic dentistry and dedicated to ongoing education.
  • Patient-Centered Care: Your comfort and satisfaction are our top priorities. Every treatment is explained clearly, and your questions are always welcome.
  • Advanced Technology: Enjoy the latest digital imaging, 3D printers, and precise bonding for exceptional results.
  • Convenient Location: Proudly serving Wauwatosa and the greater Milwaukee area for over 40 years.

Call Us at (414) 261-3376 or Call to Request an Appointment!

html:
Preventative Dentistry in Wauwatosa: Stop the Problems Before They Start

When it comes to maintaining a healthy, beautiful smile, preventative dentistry in Wauwatosa is your first line of defense. Regular visits to the dentist for preventative care can save you time, money, and unnecessary pain down the road. At MidTown Dental Care, we believe that prevention is the key to long-term oral health, and we are here to help guide you every step of the way.

Why is Preventative Dentistry Important?

Preventative dentistry in Wauwatosa is crucial because it helps you avoid painful and expensive dental procedures. It also gives you the chance to address minor issues before they turn into bigger problems. Regular teeth cleanings and exams are essential for removing plaque and tartar buildup, which can lead to tooth decay and gum disease. In addition, routine visits allow our team at MidTown Dental Care to catch potential issues early, ensuring that you get the treatment you need before they become more severe.

By staying on top of your oral health, you can enjoy a lifetime of healthy teeth and gums with minimal effort. Plus, preventative care often means fewer dental procedures overall, saving you time and money.

The Process of Preventative Dentistry in Wauwatosa

At MidTown Dental Care, we take a comprehensive approach to preventative dentistry in Wauwatosa. Here’s what you can expect during a typical visit:

  1. Initial Consultation: When you visit our office, we’ll start with a thorough evaluation of your dental health. This includes taking digital X-rays (a quick, non-invasive way to check for issues that can’t be seen with the naked eye), reviewing your medical history, and discussing any concerns or questions you have about your oral health.
  2. Professional Cleaning: Professional cleaning is one of the most important parts of preventative dentistry. Our skilled hygienists will remove plaque and tartar buildup, which can cause cavities and gum disease if left untreated. They’ll also polish your teeth, leaving you with a fresh, clean feeling.
  3. Comprehensive Examination: After your cleaning, your dentist will perform a detailed examination of your teeth and gums. We look for early signs of tooth decay, gum disease, oral cancer, and other potential issues that could affect your overall health. We also use advanced technology like our Cone Beam CT Scanner to get an in-depth view of your mouth and jaw to catch any underlying issues.
  4. Fluoride Treatment: Depending on your needs, we may recommend a fluoride treatment to help strengthen your enamel and prevent cavities. Fluoride is a natural mineral that helps remineralize your teeth, making them more resistant to decay.
  5. Personalized Care Plan: If any concerns arise during your exam, we’ll create a customized treatment plan designed to address your specific needs. Whether it’s additional teeth cleanings, sealants, or specific treatments, we’ll make sure you understand all your options.

Why Choose MidTown Dental Care for Preventative Dentistry in Wauwatosa?

Functional Benefits of Cosmetic Dentistry

  1. Corrects Bite Issues – First, cosmetic treatments can improve the alignment of your teeth, making chewing and speaking more comfortable.
  2. Strengthens Damaged Teeth – Next, crowns and veneers restore the strength of weakened or damaged teeth, preventing further issues.
  3. Reduces Teeth Grinding Discomfort – However, cosmetic procedures, like veneers, can help with teeth grinding (bruxism) and reduce associated pain.
  4. Prevents Teeth Shifting – Plus, replacing missing teeth with implants or bridges helps maintain your bite, preventing surrounding teeth from shifting.
  5. Improves Overall Oral Health – Lastly, cosmetic dentistry contributes to better long–term oral health by addressing issues like misalignment or damaged teeth.

Aesthetic Benefits of Cosmetic Dentistry

html:
Restore Your Smile with Fast, Custom Crowns at MidTown Dental Care

When a tooth breaks or is otherwise structurally unsound, a crown helps to rebuild that tooth’s shape and functionality. Crowns are essentially strong, artificial caps that appear identical to your natural tooth and are secured just on top of the tooth. They are usually made of ceramic or composite materials. The tooth in need of a crown is prepared for the procedure and 3D scanned to create a perfect digital image, which is used to construct the crown itself. At MidTown Dental Care in Milwaukee, the crown is constructed in our office, making the entire process very fast and convenient for you.

What Are CEREC Crowns? 

CEREC stands for “chairside economical restoration of esthetic ceramics” and refers to crowns that are constructed using computer design and manufacturing (also known as CAD/CAM technology). The bad-tasting impression materials are long gone and have been replaced by a convenient digital camera.  

This advanced approach to making dental crowns allows us to create and deliver a crown in just one day. You can come into our office for an appointment, we will prepare your tooth for the crown, and take a digital impression. After that, we design the crown, mill it on a milling machine, and sinter it in an oven. This entire process can be completed in under two hours.  

Why Come To MidTown Dental Care For Your CEREC Crown

At MidTown Dental Care, we pride ourselves on outstanding crown construction and placement. We create exact margins for the crowns on the tooth, so you experience an improved fit. You will also save time by being able to have your crown placed in the same appointment. Additionally, we use permanent cement for crown placement, which means you will have decreased sensitivity in comparison to the outcomes associated with other methods and materials. 

When you are able to receive a crown in a day, you also do not have to worry about the hassles of temporary crowns, such as the potential for losing the temporary crown. Instead, just come in and have your broken tooth fixed in approximately 60-90 minutes.   

Schedule An Appointment Today

If you are in immediate need of a CEREC crown, give MidTown Dental Care a call today at (414) 258-5351! But if you are looking for other types of dental care, information, or services, we offer a wide array. Beyond crowns, we also offer veneers and take impressions for partials. If you are not sure what type of dental services you might be in need of, you can schedule a preventive dentistry appointment. We will help you keep your smile healthy and beautiful through regular care and checkups.

html:
Dental Implants in Wauwatosa: Restoring Your Smile and Oral Health

Missing teeth can affect much more than the appearance of your smile. They can change the way you eat, affect how clearly you speak, contribute to bone loss, and make it harder to feel confident in everyday situations. Dental implants in Wauwatosa offer a stable, natural-looking way to replace missing teeth and rebuild your smile for the long term.

At MidTown Dental Care, we provide comprehensive dental implant care in one convenient location. Our doctors can guide you through the process from your initial evaluation and 3D imaging to bone grafting when necessary, implant placement, and your final restoration. Whether you need to replace one tooth, several teeth, or stabilize a denture, we can create a treatment plan based on your oral health, needs, and goals.

Our team includes Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego, combining decades of dental experience with advanced technology, including CBCT imaging and Yomi robot-assisted implant technology.

Ready to find out if dental implants are right for you? Schedule a dental implant consultation with MidTown Dental Care in Wauwatosa.

What Are Dental Implants?

A dental implant is a small post that is surgically placed into the jawbone to replace the root of a missing tooth. As the area heals, the implant integrates with the surrounding bone to create a strong foundation for a dental restoration.

Depending on how many teeth are missing, dental implants can support:

  • A single dental crown
  • An implant-supported bridge
  • An implant-supported denture
  • Other implant-based restorations are designed to replace multiple missing teeth

Unlike a traditional removable denture, an implant receives support from the jawbone. Because the implant replaces the missing tooth root, it can also help maintain the bone in that area of the jaw.

The result is a tooth replacement designed to look, feel, and function much like natural teeth.

Which Type of Dental Implant Treatment Is Right for Me?

There is no single dental implant solution that is right for every patient. At MidTown Dental Care, we evaluate the number and location of your missing teeth, your jawbone, gum health, bite, medical history, and treatment goals before recommending an option.

Single-Tooth Dental Implants

If you are missing one tooth, a single-tooth dental implant can replace it without relying on the neighboring teeth for support. The implant serves as the replacement root, while a custom dental crown restores the visible portion of the tooth.

This can be an excellent alternative to a traditional dental bridge for patients who want an independent replacement for one missing tooth.

Implant-Supported Bridges

If several adjacent teeth are missing, an implant-supported bridge can use strategically placed dental implants to support multiple replacement teeth.

Because the restoration is supported by implants rather than natural teeth, healthy neighboring teeth generally do not need to serve as anchors in the same way they would with a traditional tooth-supported bridge.

Implant-Supported Dentures

For patients missing many or all of their teeth, implant-supported dentures can provide greater stability than traditional removable dentures.

Dental implants provide support for the restoration, helping reduce the movement and slipping that some patients experience with conventional dentures. Depending on your needs, we can determine the appropriate implant and restoration approach during your consultation.

Why Choose Dental Implants to Replace Missing Teeth?

Dental implants have become an important tooth-replacement option because they address both the visible tooth and its underlying support.

Benefits can include:

Natural appearance. Your final restoration is designed to complement your smile and surrounding teeth.

Improved chewing ability. Stable implant-supported restorations can make eating more comfortable and predictable.

Greater confidence. Replacing visible gaps or improving the stability of a restoration can make it easier to smile, speak, and interact confidently.

Jawbone support. When a tooth is lost, the bone that previously supported its root can begin to change over time. An implant transfers forces to the surrounding bone and can help preserve bone in the area.

No reliance on adjacent teeth for a single implant. A single-tooth implant can replace a missing tooth without preparing healthy neighboring teeth to support a conventional bridge.

Long-term potential. With good oral hygiene, professional dental care, and appropriate maintenance, dental implants are designed to provide a durable tooth-replacement solution.

Complete Dental Implant Care in One Office

Dental implant treatment often involves several phases. Being able to coordinate those phases through one dental practice can make treatment simpler for patients.

At MidTown Dental Care, we provide comprehensive implant treatment from placement through restoration, including bone grafting when it is necessary to prepare the jaw for an implant.

Your treatment may include:

  1. Comprehensive implant consultation
  2. Digital imaging and evaluation
  3. Personalized implant planning
  4. Bone grafting or other preparatory treatment when needed
  5. Dental implant placement
  6. Healing and integration
  7. Final implant restoration
  8. Ongoing preventive care and implant maintenance

Keeping these stages coordinated allows our doctors to consider both the surgical and restorative aspects of your treatment from the beginning.

Advanced Dental Implant Technology: Yomi Robot-Assisted Surgery

MidTown Dental Care offers Yomi robot-assisted dental implant technology to support precise implant planning and placement.

Yomi is a robotic platform designed for dental implant surgery. Your dentist remains in control of the procedure while the system provides real-time guidance based on the digital treatment plan.

Before surgery, detailed imaging allows us to evaluate your jaw and plan factors such as the intended location, angle, and depth of the implant. During placement, Yomi provides guidance to help the dentist follow that plan.

This provider-driven technology gives our team another advanced tool for planning and performing dental implant procedures.

Patients interested in learning more can explore our dedicated Yomi Robot-Assisted Dental Implants page for information about how the technology works and what to expect.

Do I Need a Bone Graft Before Getting a Dental Implant?

Not everyone needs bone grafting before dental implant placement.

Dental implants need sufficient healthy bone for support. If a tooth has been missing for an extended period, bone volume in that area may have decreased. Bone loss can also result from periodontal disease, trauma, infection, or other factors.

During your implant evaluation, we can assess the available bone and determine whether additional preparation is necessary.

When bone grafting is recommended, MidTown Dental Care can incorporate it into your overall implant treatment plan rather than automatically sending you elsewhere for that phase of care.

Experienced Dental Implant Care in Wauwatosa

Experience, technology, and careful treatment planning all matter when considering dental implants.

MidTown Dental Care has served patients in the greater Milwaukee area for more than 40 years. Our dental team includes Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego.

Dr. Russell has practiced dentistry for more than 20 years and has a particular interest in bringing modern dental technologies into the practice. Dr. Hoyme has more than 15 years of experience and completed a general practice residency after dental school. Dr. Schmidt is a graduate of Marquette University School of Dentistry and has also completed a general practice residency at Loyola University in Chicago. Dr. Crego brings more than 40 years of dental experience to the practice and has a particular interest in implant placement, crown and bridge dentistry, and new dental technology.

Together, our doctors focus on creating treatment plans that restore not only the appearance of your smile but also its comfort and function.

How Much Do Dental Implants Cost in Wauwatosa?

There is not one universal price for dental implants because treatment varies significantly from patient to patient.

Your total cost can depend on factors such as:

  • How many teeth need to be replaced
  • Number of dental implants needed
  • Type of final restoration
  • Whether an extraction is required
  • Whether bone grafting is necessary
  • Complexity of treatment
  • Insurance benefits
  • Individual treatment needs

After evaluating your smile, our team can explain the recommended treatment and provide a personalized cost estimate.

Financing Dental Implant Treatment

We understand that dental implants are an investment in your oral health. MidTown Dental Care offers several ways to help patients manage the cost of care.

Financing options include CareCredit, Cherry, and Sunbit, as well as in-house financing for certain procedures. Please contact our team to discuss your current benefits and payment options.

Our team can review applicable benefits and payment options with you so that you understand the financial side of treatment before moving forward.

Dental Implant FAQs

Are dental implants permanent?

Dental implants are intended to be a long-term tooth-replacement solution. The implant itself can remain functional for many years with appropriate oral hygiene and professional care. The crown, bridge, or denture attached to the implant may eventually need maintenance or replacement because it experiences everyday wear.

Am I a candidate for dental implants?

Many adults with missing teeth may be candidates for implants. Important considerations include gum health, available jawbone, overall health, oral hygiene, and certain lifestyle factors. A dental implant consultation and appropriate imaging are the best ways to determine your candidacy.

Can I get a dental implant if I have bone loss?

Possibly. Bone loss does not automatically mean you cannot receive an implant. Some patients may benefit from bone grafting to increase the amount of bone available to support an implant. We can evaluate your specific situation during your consultation.

Is getting a dental implant painful?

The implant placement area is numbed during treatment to help keep you comfortable. Some soreness, swelling, or tenderness is normal after surgery, but recovery varies by patient and procedure. Our team will provide instructions for managing your recovery at home.

How long does the dental implant process take?

The timeline varies. Some patients require preliminary procedures such as extraction or bone grafting, while others may be ready for implant placement sooner. After placement, the implant typically needs time to integrate with the surrounding bone before the final restoration is completed. We will provide a more specific timeline after evaluating your needs.

Is a dental implant better than a bridge?

Neither option is universally better. A single dental implant replaces a missing tooth independently and generally does not require preparing neighboring healthy teeth. A traditional bridge can also effectively replace a missing tooth and may be appropriate in different clinical circumstances. We can explain the advantages and considerations of both based on your smile.

Can dental implants support dentures?

Yes. Dental implants can be used to support dentures and provide greater stability than a conventional removable denture. The number and placement of implants required depend on your anatomy and the type of restoration planned.

How do I take care of dental implants?

Dental implants still require excellent oral hygiene. Brush regularly, clean carefully around the implant restoration, and maintain professional dental cleanings and examinations. Depending on your restoration, our team may recommend additional cleaning tools or techniques.

Can smokers get dental implants?

Smoking does not automatically rule out dental implants, but tobacco use can interfere with healing and is associated with an increased risk of implant complications. Your dentist will review this and other health considerations when determining whether implant treatment is appropriate.

What is the first step toward getting dental implants?

The first step is a dental implant consultation. We will evaluate your teeth, gums, jawbone, health history, and goals, obtain necessary imaging, and discuss the treatment options that may work for you. You will then have an opportunity to review the proposed treatment, timeline, and financial considerations before deciding how to proceed.

Schedule a Dental Implant Consultation in Wauwatosa

You do not have to continue living with a missing tooth, uncomfortable chewing, or a restoration that no longer gives you the confidence you want.

At MidTown Dental Care, Dr. Laura Russell, Dr. AnnMarie Hoyme, Dr. Karla Schmidt, and Dr. Mark Crego provide comprehensive dental implant care using advanced technology and individualized treatment planning. From bone grafting and implant placement to your final restoration, our team can coordinate your care at our Wauwatosa dental office.

If you’re considering dental implants in Wauwatosa, schedule a consultation with MidTown Dental Care at 8726 W. North Ave., Wauwatosa, WI 53226. We’ll help you understand your options and determine the right path toward restoring your smile.

Schedule Your Dental Implant Consultationt and take the first step toward a healthier, more confident smile.

The only FDA-cleared robotic device for dental surgery

We’re proudly offering Yomi®, the only FDA-cleared robotic platform designed for dental implant surgery. Yomi tracks movements in real-time and prevents any
off-plan movements through haptic feedback and multisensory guidance. Clinical research has shown that Yomi is the most accurate modality for implant surgery.
